speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to begin our examination. To start, can you please describe the appearance and location of these skin lesions? Have you noticed any changes in their size, color, or number recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; given the daycare exposure and the timing relative to the brother's chickenpox, could you please tell me if these lesions have ever crusted over or if the child has developed any fever or malaise? Also, do the lesions look like clear, fluid-filled vesicles or more like solid bumps?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_lesions_close_up

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital_Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98°F), Blood_Pressure 90/60 mmHg, Heart_Rate 100 bpm, Respiratory_Rate 20 breaths/min. Dermatology Inspection: Multiple skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. Dermatology Palpation: Lesions are firm, without warmth or erythema. CBC: WBC 6,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 12 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL. Patient History: Lesions have not crusted over; no fever or malaise reported. Lesion Appearance: Solid bumps (pearly papules), not clear, fluid-filled vesicles.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I must clarify that the symptoms you described—skin-colored, nontender pearly papules with central umbilication—are classic for Molluscum Contagiosum, not acute appendicitis. To confirm this and rule out other viral exanthems, have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever, fatigue, or swollen lymph nodes recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential
DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
